title: Overspend by campaign
prompt: Finance wants to see which campaigns spend more than planned. Write `solve(budgets)` so it returns, for every campaign, how many days it has, on how many of them it went over plan, and by how much in total.
rules: A day is over plan when `actual_spend` is more than `planned_spend`. Spending exactly the plan isn't over.
`days` counts every row of the campaign; `days_over` counts the days over plan.
`overspend` adds up `actual_spend - planned_spend` on the days over plan only. A campaign never over plan has `overspend` 0.
Return one row for every campaign, even one that was never over: `campaign_id`, `days`, `days_over`, `overspend`.
hints: Group by `campaign_id` and put the condition inside each aggregate, rather than filtering first.
A filter before `groupBy` would drop the campaigns that were never over.
For `overspend`, sum `F.when(over, F.col("actual_spend") - F.col("planned_spend")).otherwise(0)`: the `otherwise(0)` is what makes it 0 instead of NULL.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(budgets):
    # One row per campaign: days, days_over and overspend.
    return budgets
